inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (SBC add-back $27.9M) + equity-award withholding taxes $12.8M from kpis (equity_award_taxes, FY2025); AVY discloses no single combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation line for SBC, so the two cash-flow-statement lines are summed
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q); annual_share_growth_pct held at 0.0 despite a persistent buyback program (84.1M FY2021 -> 76.4M Q2 2026) because SBC is fully expensed in the flows -- the buyback cash IS the mechanism funding the flat count, and charging both would double-count (see sbc-flat-share-count memory note)
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAPM: risk-free 4.2% (10yr UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.15 (materials/industrials, moderately cyclical) -> cost of equity ~9.95%. After-tax cost of debt 5.0% x (1-24%) = 3.8%. Capital weights from market cap $13.0B / total debt $3.68B (E 78%, D 22%) -> WACC ~8.6%, rounded to base 8.5%. Bull 8.0% (lower execution/leverage risk in the high-value-mix success case), bear 9.5% (leverage plus tariff/trade-policy risk premium) -- risk charged once via scenario-specific WACC, not stacked again on top of the probability weights
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- AVY's lease liabilities are small relative to total debt and are excluded from net debt; no separate lease adjustment applied
inputs.nci_treatment: not applicable -- AVY has no disclosed material noncontrolling interest
inputs.notes: Owner-FCF component DCF per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/references/owner-fcf.md. Routed as a standard US operating company (materials science / digital identification manufacturer), not a REIT/bank/LIC, so no adaptations file needed. AVY is a NET-DEBT company (net debt $3.45B vs FCF base ~$0.7B), not net-cash, so the interest-income-stripping rule (section 1b) does not apply -- interest_income is 0 by construction, not by adjustment. SBC is genuinely small for this business (~0.46% of revenue, an industrial manufacturer, not a tech/SaaS company) so house and street bases are close but not identical (band_position is meaningful, not degenerate). 10-year horizon used because FY2025's actual owner-FCF margin (7.6%) sits below the component-built margin path (10.3% in year 1, ramping to ~11.4% by year 10) as the 2028 EBITDA-margin target (17%+, vs FY2025's disclosed 16.4% adjusted EBITDA margin) phases in and FY2025's unusually large working-capital/tariff-related cash drag (reported FCF conversion depressed by an estimated ~$130-190M vs a component-clean build) normalizes -- the margin has not yet matured within a 5-year window. Capex modeled slightly above FY2025's depressed 1.91%-of-revenue actual (which reflects a multi-year capex pause) toward a more normal 2.0-2.3% mid-cycle rate for a materials manufacturer. Working capital modeled with a NEGATIVE capture rate (-12% base) because AVY is a manufacturer/distributor whose receivables + inventory structurally exceed payables, so revenue growth consumes cash -- the opposite sign from a prepaid-subscription business. FY2020 full-year figures are missing from metrics_normalized (only quarterly/H1 rows populated), so 5-year historical CAGRs use FY2019 as the base year instead of FY2020, spanning a 5-6yr window; this is noted because it avoids the COVID-distorted FY2020 print rather than compounding around it.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2019->FY2024, since FY2020 full-year figures are missing from metrics_normalized); equity CAGR (13.94% 5yr) is inflated by the 2021-2022 margin/pricing surge off a low COVID-era equity base and diverges >30% from revenue, so revenue CAGR is used as the more representative anchor rather than equity per the default hierarchy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (13.94%) diverges materially (>3x) from revenue 5yr CAGR (4.37%) and EPS 5yr CAGR (19.58%) similarly overstated -- both reflect FY2019's depressed equity/EPS base (pre-pandemic, pre the FY2021-22 margin recovery and Vestcom-driven mix shift) rather than a repeatable growth rate; base-case growth path is anchored to guided organic growth (3-4% FY2026, 5%+ by 2028) and revenue CAGR, not the equity or EPS CAGRs.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF 5yr CAGR (7.06%) is close to reported FCF 5yr CAGR (6.73%) -- SBC is a small share of revenue for this industrial manufacturer (~0.46%), so the SBC adjustment does not materially change the growth story, unlike SBC-heavy tech names.

base.narrative: FY2026 growth 3.5% (low end of the 3-4% guided organic range, reflecting the disclosed Q3 2026 pre-buy unwind headwind), accelerating to 5% by years 4-5 as the high-value-category mix (Intelligent Labels/RFID, Vestcom, Embelex, Specialty & Durable Labels -- already nearing half of sales) reaches and briefly exceeds the 2028 5%+ organic-growth target, then decelerating toward a 2.5% terminal rate as the business matures and the mix-shift tailwind is largely captured. EBITDA margin ramps from FY2025's disclosed 16.4% to the 2028 17%+ target by year 5-6 and holds at 17.5% thereafter on continued productivity programs. Cash tax rate held near AVY's actual ~23.6% effective cash rate (no valuation-allowance distortion to ramp away), nudged to 24.5% long-run for a modestly more conservative multinational blend.

bull.narrative: High-value categories (Intelligent Labels/RFID, Vestcom, Embelex, architectural films) scale faster than the 2028 targets as Walmart/Kroger-style RFID retail rollouts broaden beyond the initial partners and the new Wiliot ambient-IoT stake opens an adjacent growth vector; the 2028 5%+ growth / 17%+ EBITDA-margin targets are hit a year early and the mix shift keeps pushing margin toward 18.5% as Materials Group commodity exposure keeps shrinking as a share of the portfolio. Tariff/trade headwinds prove transitory and apparel destocking reverses.

bear.narrative: Tariff and trade-policy escalation persists well beyond 2026, compounding the already-disclosed low-single-digit apparel sales headwind; commodity Materials Group pricing competition (UPM Raflatac, CCL Industries) erodes margin faster than productivity programs can offset; RFID/Intelligent Labels rollout stalls as the concentrated Walmart/Kroger retailer base slows adoption pace; the Q3 2026 pre-buy unwind proves to be the start of a longer demand air-pocket rather than a one-quarter timing effect, and elevated leverage (D/E ~1.6x) constrains the bolt-on M&A the high-value-category strategy depends on. 2028 targets are missed.

scenario_narratives.base: Guided FY2026 organic growth (3-4%) decelerating near-term on the disclosed Q3 pre-buy unwind, then accelerating toward the 2028 5%+ organic-growth / 17%+ EBITDA-margin targets as high-value categories (Intelligent Labels, Vestcom, Embelex, Specialty & Durable Labels) continue approaching half of total sales, before settling to a mature 2.5% terminal growth rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: High-value-category mix shift and RFID/ambient-IoT (Wiliot) expansion outrun the 2028 targets; tariff headwinds prove transitory.
scenario_narratives.bear: Persistent tariff/trade escalation, commodity Materials Group pricing pressure, and a stalled RFID retailer rollout cause the 2028 targets to be missed and margin to compress rather than expand.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 shifted to 20/50/30. Bear weight raised above the house default because the bear axis (tariff/trade escalation, commodity Materials pricing, and RFID rollout dependency on a small number of large retail partners) is a real, currently-live risk explicitly flagged in management's own guidance assumptions -- not a tail scenario -- and leverage (D/E ~1.6x, net debt/EBITDA ~2.3x) leaves less room to absorb a prolonged downturn without curtailing buybacks. Bull weight trimmed correspondingly because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously (RFID rollout broadening beyond Walmart/Kroger, the new and unproven Wiliot stake paying off, and tariff pressure reversing) rather than one clean catalyst.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Avery Dennison is valued on a strict owner-FCF component DCF: FY2025 actual revenue ($8,855.5M) as the base, with EBITDA margin ramping from FY2025's disclosed 16.4% adjusted EBITDA margin toward management's own 2028 targets (5%+ organic growth, 17%+ EBITDA margin) unveiled at the September 23, 2026 Investor Showcase, then held flat at a modestly higher mature level. SBC is fully expensed (it is genuinely small for this industrial manufacturer, ~0.46% of revenue) and the share count is held flat at the latest diluted count (76.4M, Q2 2026) -- the company's substantial buyback program ($572.3M in FY2025) is the cash mechanism funding that flat count, not a source of incremental per-share value on top of the SBC charge. AVY carries net debt (~$3.45B), not net cash, so no interest-income adjustment applies. A 10-year horizon is used because the FY2025 actual owner-FCF margin (7.6%) sits meaningfully below the component-built path (which starts at ~10.3% and matures near 11.4%) while the 2028 margin target phases in and an unusually large FY2025 working-capital/tariff-related cash drag normalizes -- capitalizing an immature margin at year 5 would understate the business. Working capital is modeled with a negative capture rate, consistent with a manufacturer/distributor whose receivables and inventory structurally exceed payables.
key_risks_to_valuation: Q3 2026 disclosed ~$0.50 sequential EPS headwind as the Q2 customer pre-buy unwinds -- a near-term print that could read as deceleration even if the multi-year trajectory is intact
Tariff/trade-policy escalation, already producing a measurable low-single-digit apparel sales headwind through 2025-2026
Commodity Materials Group pricing competition limits pricing power outside high-value niches, capping the pace of the margin-mix shift
RFID/Intelligent Labels growth is concentrated in a small number of large retail partners (Walmart, Kroger); a slowdown there directly hits the highest-growth part of the bull case
Leverage (D/E ~1.6x, net debt/EBITDA ~2.3x) constrains capacity for the bolt-on M&A the high-value-category strategy has relied on, without additional equity or debt
